qualifying_produce.sourceText:
An agricultural household for 77th Round survey was defined as a household receiving
value of produce more than Rs. 4000/- from agricultural activities (e.g., cultivation of field
crops, horticultural crops, fodder crops, plantation, animal husbandry, poultry, fishery,
piggery, bee-keeping, vermiculture, sericulture, etc.) and having at least one member self-
employed in agriculture either in the principal status or in subsidiary status during last 365
days

definition_days.sourceText:
An agricultural household for 77th Round survey was defined as a household receiving
value of produce more than Rs. 4000/- from agricultural activities (e.g., cultivation of field
crops, horticultural crops, fodder crops, plantation, animal husbandry, poultry, fishery,
piggery, bee-keeping, vermiculture, sericulture, etc.) and having at least one member self-
employed in agriculture either in the principal status or in subsidiary status during last 365
days

plates.title: Wages bring in more than crops for the average farm household
plates.vintageNote: The API does not publish a data revision date. The report edition date and archive capture date are separate provenance and do not establish the API revision date.
plates.source: MoSPI, NSS 77th round, Situation Assessment of Agricultural Households
plates.sub: Average monthly income per agricultural household by source, in rupees, over the agricultural year.
plates.explain: Each source is net of the cash the household paid out for it. Pensions and money sent home by family members elsewhere are shown, but the survey leaves them out of its income total.

rows.name: Pensions and money sent home (outside the total)

plates.title: Income climbs steeply with land above a hectare
plates.vintageNote: The API does not publish a data revision date. The report edition date and archive capture date are separate provenance and do not establish the API revision date.
plates.source: MoSPI, NSS 77th round, Situation Assessment of Agricultural Households
plates.sub: Average monthly income per agricultural household by land possessed, in rupees.
plates.explain: Households with almost no land live mostly on wages, which is why they earn more than those with a small plot. Above a hectare, crop income takes over.

plates.title: Below a hectare, wages matter more than crops
plates.vintageNote: The API does not publish a data revision date. The report edition date and archive capture date are separate provenance and do not establish the API revision date.
plates.source: MoSPI, NSS 77th round, Situation Assessment of Agricultural Households
plates.sub: Average monthly wage and crop income per agricultural household by land possessed, in rupees.
plates.explain: Read the two halves together: wages stay roughly level across land sizes, while crop income rises with the land a household holds.

plates.title: Counting the family’s own labour and inputs shrinks the return from farming
plates.vintageNote: The API does not publish a data revision date. The report edition date and archive capture date are separate provenance and do not establish the API revision date.
plates.source: MoSPI, NSS 77th round, Situation Assessment of Agricultural Households
plates.sub: Average monthly income per agricultural household, with and without a value put on the family’s own labour, seed and feed, in rupees.
plates.explain: Valuing the family’s own inputs is not another cash payment. It shows what farming earns after paying for everything the household itself supplies, which matters most for animals, where family labour does most of the work.

plates.title: Scheduled Caste farm households earn the least
plates.vintageNote: The API does not publish a data revision date. The report edition date and archive capture date are separate provenance and do not establish the API revision date.
plates.source: MoSPI, NSS 77th round, Situation Assessment of Agricultural Households
plates.sub: Average monthly income per agricultural household by social group, in rupees.
plates.explain: An average hides the spread inside each group. Differences in land held explain part of the gap between groups.

plates.title: Farm household income varies widely between states
plates.vintageNote: The API does not publish a data revision date. The report edition date and archive capture date are separate provenance and do not establish the API revision date.
plates.source: MoSPI, NSS 77th round, Situation Assessment of Agricultural Households
plates.sub: Average monthly income per agricultural household, in rupees, by state.
plates.explain: State figures rest on smaller samples than the all-India figure. The survey groups the smaller north-eastern states and the union territories.

plates.title: Hired labour and fertiliser are the largest cash costs of growing crops
plates.group: What farming costs, and what animals earn
plates.vintageNote: The API does not publish a data revision date. The report edition date and archive capture date are separate provenance and do not establish the API revision date.
plates.source: MoSPI, NSS 77th round, Situation Assessment of Agricultural Households
plates.sub: Average monthly cash spent on crop production per household that grows crops, in rupees.
plates.explain: These are cash payments only. The family’s own labour and saved seed are not in this chart.

plates.title: Milk earns most of what animals bring in
plates.group: What farming costs, and what animals earn
plates.vintageNote: The date identifies the published Report 587 edition, not an assertion about later undocumented file revisions.
plates.source: MoSPI, NSS 77th round, Situation Assessment of Agricultural Households
plates.sub: Average monthly receipts from animals per household that keeps them, in rupees, before costs.
plates.explain: These are gross receipts. Feed is by far the largest cash cost of keeping animals; the costs are in Every Cut.

plates.title: Most farm households possess less than a hectare
plates.vintageNote: The API does not publish a data revision date. The report edition date and archive capture date are separate provenance and do not establish the API revision date.
plates.source: MoSPI, NSS 77th round, Situation Assessment of Agricultural Households
plates.sub: Estimated number of agricultural households by land possessed.
plates.explain: Land possessed includes land owned, land leased in and land otherwise held, less land leased out. It is the land a household can farm.

plates.title: Land is mostly leased for fixed cash or a share of the crop
plates.vintageNote: The API does not publish a data revision date. The report edition date and archive capture date are separate provenance and do not establish the API revision date.
plates.source: MoSPI, NSS 77th round, Situation Assessment of Agricultural Households
plates.sub: Share of land leased out under each kind of lease, per cent.
plates.explain: Shares of the leased area. Leases from relatives often carry no fixed rent at all.

rows.name: From relatives, no fixed terms, July–December 2018
From relatives, no fixed terms, January–June 2019

plates.title: Most paddy is sold in the local market
plates.vintageNote: The API does not publish a data revision date. The report edition date and archive capture date are separate provenance and do not establish the API revision date.
plates.source: MoSPI, NSS 77th round, Situation Assessment of Agricultural Households
plates.sub: Of every 1,000 kilograms of paddy sold, how much went to each buyer.
plates.explain: The kharif paddy crop of 2018. The local market includes traders and private buyers in the village and the nearest town.

plates.title: When a sale disappoints, the price is usually the reason
plates.vintageNote: The API does not publish a data revision date. The report edition date and archive capture date are separate provenance and do not establish the API revision date.
plates.source: MoSPI, NSS 77th round, Situation Assessment of Agricultural Households
plates.sub: Paddy-selling households per 1,000, by how they felt about the sale.
plates.explain: The households’ own account of the sale. A price below the market is what the seller believed, not a measured gap.

plates.title: Most paddy and wheat sellers did not know the support price
plates.vintageNote: The date identifies the published Report 587 edition, not an assertion about later undocumented file revisions.
plates.source: MoSPI, NSS 77th round, Situation Assessment of Agricultural Households
plates.sub: Paddy and wheat sellers per 1,000 who knew the minimum support price, knew the agency that buys at it, and sold to that agency.
plates.explain: The minimum support price (MSP) is the price at which government agencies buy. Knowing it is a long way from selling at it.

rows.name: Paddy sellers who knew the MSP
Paddy sellers who knew the procurement agency
Paddy sellers who sold to the agency
Wheat sellers who knew the MSP
Wheat sellers who knew the procurement agency
Wheat sellers who sold to the agency

plates.title: Few farmers insure their crops
plates.vintageNote: The API does not publish a data revision date. The report edition date and archive capture date are separate provenance and do not establish the API revision date.
plates.source: MoSPI, NSS 77th round, Situation Assessment of Agricultural Households
plates.sub: Paddy and wheat growers per 1,000, by whether they insured the crop.
plates.explain: A farmer who takes a crop loan from a bank is usually insured with it. Insuring by choice means buying cover on top of that, or without a loan.

rows.name: Paddy, insured only through a crop loan
Wheat, insured only through a crop loan

plates.title: Not knowing about insurance is the commonest reason for going without
plates.vintageNote: The date identifies the published Report 587 edition, not an assertion about later undocumented file revisions.
plates.source: MoSPI, NSS 77th round, Situation Assessment of Agricultural Households
plates.sub: Paddy growers who did not insure, per 1,000, by their main reason.
plates.explain: Each household gave one main reason. The two kinds of not knowing are separate answers in the survey.

rows.name: Did not know about crop insurance
Did not know it was available to them

plates.title: Drought causes most paddy losses
plates.vintageNote: The API does not publish a data revision date. The report edition date and archive capture date are separate provenance and do not establish the API revision date.
plates.source: MoSPI, NSS 77th round, Situation Assessment of Agricultural Households
plates.sub: Paddy growers who lost part of the crop, per 1,000, by the cause of the loss.
plates.explain: Only households that lost part of their paddy crop are counted here.

plates.title: Commercial banks lend the most; professional moneylenders come next
plates.period: Loans outstanding at the first interview, January–August 2019
plates.vintageNote: The date identifies the published Report 587 edition, not an assertion about later undocumented file revisions.
plates.source: MoSPI, NSS 77th round, Situation Assessment of Agricultural Households
plates.sub: Of every ₹1,000 that agricultural households owe, how much is owed to each kind of lender.
plates.explain: These shares divide the money owed, not the households. Insurers, provident funds, employers, chit funds and self-help groups not linked to banks hold the remainder.

plates.title: Bigger farms carry far bigger loans
plates.period: Loans outstanding at the first interview, January–August 2019
plates.vintageNote: The date identifies the published Report 587 edition, not an assertion about later undocumented file revisions.
plates.source: MoSPI, NSS 77th round, Situation Assessment of Agricultural Households
plates.sub: Average outstanding loan per agricultural household by land possessed, in rupees.
plates.explain: The average includes households that owe nothing. Larger farms borrow more for machinery, inputs and land.

plates.title: The more land a household holds, the likelier it is to owe money
plates.period: Loans outstanding at the first interview, January–August 2019
plates.vintageNote: The date identifies the published Report 587 edition, not an assertion about later undocumented file revisions.
plates.source: MoSPI, NSS 77th round, Situation Assessment of Agricultural Households
plates.sub: Agricultural households with an outstanding loan per 1,000 households, by land possessed.
plates.explain: Land is collateral: households with more of it can borrow more easily from banks.

plates.title: Debt per farm household varies widely between states
plates.period: Loans outstanding at the first interview, January–August 2019
plates.vintageNote: The date identifies the published Report 587 edition, not an assertion about later undocumented file revisions.
plates.source: MoSPI, NSS 77th round, Situation Assessment of Agricultural Households
plates.sub: Average outstanding loan per agricultural household, in rupees, by state.
plates.explain: State figures rest on smaller samples than the all-India figure. The average includes households with no loan.
